A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same randomized-midpoint sampling work. The main text, equations, algorithms and Appendices A-D are readable and matchable despite the shortened title and localized revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, convergence guarantees and proofs, including in its appendices, but no original experiments, simulations or data analyses. Empirical findings discussed are attributed to other works.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper throughout the main text and appendices. It introduces no original empirical outcomes; references to empirical findings concern cited works.

M1.justification: The sequential and parallel randomized-midpoint predictor-corrector procedures and the log-concave sampler are unchanged. Algorithms 1-11 retain their steps and components.

E1.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates datasets or tasks. Both retain the same theoretical settings: sequential and parallel diffusion sampling and log-concave sampling.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The citation correction from [AHL+23] to [SBE+24] in Section 3.5 changes attribution, not an experimentally evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. The algorithmic step sizes and iteration budgets are theoretical parameter choices and remain unchanged.

E4.justification: No original ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, error analyses or case studies are added or removed. The appendices remain mathematical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Revisions to expectations in theoretical inequalities concern mathematics, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. The main theoretical sampling guarantees, including the d^(5/12) dimension dependence and parallel-round bounds, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the score-difference sign in the proof of Lemma A.2, adds an expectation on the initial-error term in Lemma 3.3, and explicitly requires equal initial conditions in Lemma D.2. These are local mathematical repairs; the principal theorems and complexity rates are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: improved dimension dependence for diffusion and log-concave sampling, and provable parallel diffusion sampling. The rewritten abstract does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 expands the existing score-accuracy limitation. V2 explicitly compares against [CCL+23a], emphasizes the significance of the result even with exact scores, and contrasts its requirement with the stronger epsilon/sqrt(d) requirement attributed to another research line. The smoothness limitation remains.

D1.justification: The algorithm pseudocode and theoretical parameter prescriptions are retained. Neither version adds implementation settings, hardware information, measured runtimes, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dou et al. [DCWY24] on consistency diffusion models to the discussion of score-error assumptions. Section 3.5 also corrects the sliding-window parallel-sampling attribution from [AHL+23] to [SBE+24]. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The title drops 'based', the abstract opening is rewritten, and Section 4 becomes 'Discussion and Future Work' with an expanded discussion. Smaller wording and acknowledgment edits occur, while the overall section and appendix organization is preserved.

P2.justification: Algorithm 4 moves after its introductory paragraph, and Algorithm 6 moves below the Section A.3 heading and introduction. Internal cross-reference colors and local page layout also change. No figures or result tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical precision through local corrections, including the sign in Lemma A.2 and the initialization condition in Lemma D.2. It also fixes a prior-work attribution and better explains the score-accuracy tradeoff. These are useful, limited improvements; the algorithms and main theoretical results remain unchanged.
